promo-pat-seam.title: Canva will not show you the seam #shorts
promo-pat-seam.description:
The canvas edge in Canva is a crop, not a wrap. Anything you push past the edge is cut off there, and nothing appears on the other side to continue it.

Which means you can build a pattern that looks completely finished on your screen, export it, tile it, and watch a hard grid of seams appear — straight lines through your design every tile width, where the motifs stop dead at the boundary.

And Canva will not show you that seam. There is no offset preview, no tile preview, no wrap mode. The design looks perfect right up until it is on fabric.

promo-pat-offset.title: Typed numbers. Never dragged. #shorts
promo-pat-offset.description:
Select the motif, Position, Advanced, and read the X value. Say the tile is 1200 pixels wide and the motif sits at X of 1140. Duplicate it and set the duplicate's X to 1140 minus 1200 — which is minus 60. Negative. It sits mostly off the canvas to the left with exactly the missing piece showing.

Leave Y alone. Both copies must share it exactly. Same rule vertically: Y minus the canvas height for anything crossing the top or bottom.

And a motif in a corner needs four copies — the original, one at X minus width, one at Y minus height, and one with both. Miss the fourth and you get a seam at every corner point, which is the most noticeable kind.

promo-pat-test.title: The only honest seam test #shorts
promo-pat-test.description:
You cannot check a seam inside Canva. There is no tile preview, and your eye is not going to catch a two-pixel misalignment on a square you have been staring at for an hour.

So export and tile it. Download as PNG, make a second Canva design at exactly twice the tile size, and drop the PNG in four times — at 0 and 0, 0 and 1200, 1200 and 0, and 1200 and 1200. Typed, again.

Then look at the two lines where they meet. Any motif that crosses a join should continue perfectly. Any stripe of background colour, any sliced leaf, any shift in tone — that is a seam, and it will print. Fix it in the original, export again, re-test.

promo-pat-colour.title: One correct tile is five products #shorts
promo-pat-colour.description:
Once a tile is genuinely seamless, the seams do not care what colour anything is. So duplicate the page, select the background, change it. Select the motifs, recolour them. The geometry is untouched, which means the tile is still seamless — you have not moved anything.

Five colourways from one correct tile: a neutral, a dark, a bright, a pastel, and one seasonal.

This is also why the arithmetic is worth doing properly the first time. Get one tile right and every variation inherits it. Get it slightly wrong and you have just made five broken products instead of one.
